the resting tension (force per cross-sectional area) of single frog atrial cells increases as the sarcomere length increases, and the increase in resting tension is much smaller than the increase in resting force (force per length) of the cell, indicating that the resting tension resides primarily in the structures external to the cell.
the resting tension (force per unit cross-sectional area) of intact frog atrium is about 30-fold less when determined in single intact cells than in intact tissue preparations.

1) the resting tension (and resting stress) of single frog atrial cells is dependent on the sarcomere length, 2) the resting tension of single frog atrium cells is about 8-30 times less than that reported for intact frog heart tissue, and 3) the resting tension in the intact frog heart resides primarily in structures (colla gen, elastin) outside the individual cardiac cells.
